source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use one resting heart-rate range for infants and older children because age has little effect on normal values.","B":"Interpret by age because infants normally have faster resting heart rates than older children and teenagers.","C":"Expect resting heart rate to rise with age, making higher values more typical in older children than infants.","D":"Apply adult resting limits after infancy because pediatric resting rates quickly become equivalent to adult values."}}
source_row.rationale: The American Heart Association notes that normal resting heart rate differs by pediatric age: infants average substantially faster rates than older children and teenagers. Option B correctly applies age-dependent interpretation. Option A incorrectly treats pediatric ages as sharing one range. Option C reverses the normal age trend. Option D incorrectly assumes adult limits apply soon after infancy.
